hero_section.title: Prototyping & Wireframing
hero_section.subtitle: Visualize and Validate Before You Build
hero_section.description: Save time, reduce development costs, and align your stakeholders with interactive prototypes and structural blueprints that bring your software ideas to life without writing a single line of code.

introduction_section.heading: What is
content: Think of wireframing as the architectural blueprint of a house, and prototyping as a 3D walkthrough before the foundation is poured. Wireframes establish the core layout, information architecture, and basic functionality of your app or website.

Prototypes take those wireframes and make them interactive. At Devisgon, we create clickable models that simulate the final product's user experience. This allows you to test logic, gather user feedback, and secure investor funding long before you commit to expensive backend development.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “Failing on paper is cheap. Failing in code is expensive.”

case_study_section.headline: Saving $40,000 in development costs before writing code

problem.label: Problem
problem.text: A healthcare startup wanted to build a complex patient portal but wasn't sure if elderly users would understand the navigation.

solution.label: Solution
solution.text: We built a high-fidelity prototype and ran usability tests with their target demographic, uncovering a major flaw in the appointment scheduling flow.

result.label: Result
result.text: By fixing the flow in the prototype phase, the client avoided a post-launch rewrite, saving an estimated 4 weeks of dev time and $40,000.

faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.subtitle: Get answers about wireframes and prototypes

questions.question: Can't we just jump straight into coding?
questions.answer: Jumping into code without a prototype is like building a house without a blueprint. It often leads to disjointed user experiences, endless revisions, and inflated development costs. Prototyping ensures you know exactly what to build before you build it.

questions.question: What is the difference between low-fidelity and high-fidelity?
questions.answer: Low-fidelity wireframes are simple, black-and-white sketches that focus purely on layout and structure. High-fidelity prototypes look and feel exactly like the final, polished app, complete with your brand colors, actual images, and clickable buttons.

questions.question: Can I use a prototype to pitch to investors?
questions.answer: Absolutely! A high-fidelity, clickable prototype is one of the most powerful tools for fundraising. It allows investors to 'use' your product and understand your vision clearly without you needing to spend tens of thousands on actual development.

questions.question: Does a prototype actually work with real data?
questions.answer: Usually, no. Prototypes use 'dummy data' and simulated interactions to look and feel real. They do not have a functional backend database or live API connections—that part comes during the actual development phase.
